## Preservation and spoilage

**Source:** blood/organs 1–4 hours, essence 30 minutes–2 hours unless contained, meat 8–24 hours, hides 12–24 hours before curing; dry bone/horn/teeth/mineral and ordinary construct parts can last indefinitely. Active cores are exceptions. **Completion:** the manifest fixes the interval before harvesting. Where no more specific interval is stated, use the conservative low end: organs/blood 1 hour, essence 30 minutes, meat 8 hours, hide 12 hours. The clock starts when the creature dies or the material leaves its sustaining environment, not when the player finally harvests it.

Track condition separately from material tier and rarity: Fresh → Degraded → Spoiled. At one unprotected interval the lot becomes Degraded: its unit value halves and it cannot meet a recipe calling for Fresh ingredients, but otherwise retains its exact tier/properties. At two unprotected intervals it is Spoiled, value zero and unusable as an ordinary recipe ingredient or edible food. A specific recipe may explicitly require spoiled material. No new poison, curse or disease is inferred. Dividing, trading, repackaging, recovering or reharvesting a lot cannot reset its elapsed age. The label quality here is preservation condition, never an equipment grade or crafting outcome.

Work on a perishable ingredient must begin while it is eligible; ordinary reservation does not suspend aging. An exact recipe card may say its first processing phase stabilizes the input; otherwise it must remain eligible through completion. A generic engine cannot promise a 160-hour potion made from an untreated one-hour organ will succeed. This makes the card's storage/processing details mandatory.

If a required reserved component ceases to satisfy its recipe requirement before completion and no completed recipe phase expressly stabilized it, pause the order before further active work. Before resuming, the lead may reserve a fresh legal component satisfying that same requirement, including an already-legal substitution. The replacement lot keeps its own identity and age. Completed active-work phases remain completed, but any component already physically consumed or irreversibly processed before becoming unusable remains spent. If no legal replacement is supplied, abandon the order under the normal abandonment rule; do not make a completion or quality roll.

The following new mundane preservation procedure supplies a usable default without inventing magical stasis. For each lot of at most 10 lb of eligible blood/organs, meat or hide, spend 30 active minutes, a suitable trade kit, a sealable appropriately sized container, and 1 gp/0.5 lb of preservative supplies (salt, clean packing and the appropriate nonmagical stabilizer). These supplies have no independent combat or magical effect. Alchemy handles specimens, Cooking handles food, and Skinning handles hide. Make one DC 10 check using the trade's normal ability/proficiency, no assistants or quality-yield table. Success pauses spoilage for 24 elapsed hours; failure uses the supplies and time but gives no extension. This treatment must finish before the lot becomes Spoiled. It does not restore Fresh condition or remove existing age.

On a successful treatment, freeze accumulated unprotected age and resume it after the 24 hours. A replacement treatment takes the same cost/time and extends protection from its completion to 24 hours later, never adding stacked days. Any actual container breach, contamination or incompatible heat ends protection; merely opening to portion with clean tools for less than a minute does not. Preserved supplies and container mass count as cargo until discarded or used. Processing into food is not automatically safe if the source explicitly says otherwise.

Mundane specimen jars alone contain fluids but do not pause decay. They do not stabilize magical essence or active cores. Those require a separately defined compatible containment method with its own lifetime, capacity and costs; without one, the printed/default clock continues. Dry durable materials remain indefinite only while kept dry and physically intact. No generic refrigeration, freezing or stasis benefit is inferred from a spell name; its actual reviewed effect must support the storage method.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Food mass and the food ledger
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Food mass and the food ledger

One finished serving contains exactly **2/3 lb edible food**, excluding its container. Full consumption supplies **1/3 of a Small/Medium daily food requirement** or **1/6 of a Large daily food requirement**. Three ordinary servings match the reviewed 2-lb daily ration; six provide twice that food for Large. This is an explicitly authored game accounting convention, not a physiological claim. Other size/anatomy profiles keep their actual dietary requirements rather than gaining invented daily demand from this table. A creature that does not require food can still receive legally applicable meal magic through a compatible consumption route, but unused nutrition does not transfer to others.

This is **food credit only**. It grants no water, fuel, camp consumables or complete Supply Unit. Record food actually consumed separately from the still-open expedition food/water-to-Supply conversion. Food counted as a recipe input or supplement cannot also remain an uneaten ration or pay another meal/Supply entry. Food credit is still real when feast magic is declined, its shield loses comparison or an independent magical rider is blocked. Mere tasting or incomplete consumption grants no fractionated recipe benefit under this overlay.

Each card identifies its credited nutritious input mass. This reviewed overlay credits these ordinary food inputs after actual recipe preparation: **Meat, Milk, Fruit, Vegetables, Flour, Butter, Honey, Sugar, Eggs, food-grade cooking Oil, and the named Bear, Fire, Poisonous, Quetzalcoatlus, Sea and Vulture meat inputs**. The last group is treated as meat under the successful recipe's neutralization rule. Source Oil here must be actual food-grade cooking oil, not lamp fuel.

All other inputs remain required real ingredients but receive **zero credited nutritive bulk in these cards**: water, salt, wine, spices/herbs used as seasonings, bones, sinew, blood samples, marrow, bark, living root, pollen, petals, eyes, trophies, ichor, goo and bloodstones. This conservative accounting does not pronounce every such material forever inedible; a later exact edible profile may qualify it. Source names, magical properties and possible-donor lists alone cannot create nutrition. No numerical tier or monetary value substitutes for food mass.

For Standard output without catalyst retention, supplementary ordinary ration-equivalent food required is:

`ceil to 0.01 lb(max(0, 2 × Standard servings / 3 − credited source food mass))`.

Before any completion check, reserve enough for **maximum Masterwork yield floor(1.5Q)** after the **worst legal one-unit nutritive catalyst return**. The cards show that conservative maximum. A non-nutritive catalyst does not reduce the nutritious mass. A nutritive catalyst that is returned cannot simultaneously feed the meal. Selecting a different catalyst or lower yield never increases the maximum requirement. Food is supplementary and replaces none of the recipe's exact component amounts, tiers, properties, roles or forms.

Use the reviewed ration reference of **5 sp per 2 lb = 25 cp/lb**. Apply actual supplier quotes and ordinary transaction rounding once; owned real rations need not be repurchased. Preserve the immutable source economy and separately record extra food/storage acquisition. A small rounded surplus remains process waste when actually incorporated. Supplementary food is reserved before the completion check but remains separate ordinary inventory until the crafting outcome and actual catalyst return are known. **After resolving that result, and before creating any finished serving**, incorporate only the exact supplementary amount required for the resolved finished quantity and catalyst choice. Reservation alone never consumes or transforms it. A generic Failed or Mishap result creating no finished serving leaves all supplementary food unincorporated and in inventory; source inputs still follow their actual failure/recovery rules. A specific recipe that creates a failed finished product incorporates only the food actually required for that product, spending it as a product input. A later recipe may require earlier incorporation only by explicit rule. Recipe-633 currently needs no supplemental food, so its contaminated product numbers are unchanged. Reserved disposition capacity and food cannot be pledged to simultaneous work orders. Source ingredients do not become refundable merely because no supplement was needed.

Excess legal process mass is waste, with no automatic extra ration, bonus serving, salvage goods, resale value or Supply. Added ordinary water may serve the actual process but gives no nutritional offset. Source work tools are not food. All 44 current source recipes have no vessel or nonconsumed component rows; their required kitchen implements remain actual separate reusable tools.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Cooking, stabilization and storage
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Cooking, stabilization and storage

The first **15 active minutes** are the cooking/binding phase within the existing recipe work. Maintain actual heat, Cook's utensils and the printed station, knife, pot/pan and other requirements. Perishable ingredients must remain legal until binding completes. Pauses, replacement of illegal inputs and abandonment follow the shared framework. A genuinely eligible time-reduction feature scales this phase with the whole work order, rounding the phase up to a whole minute without adding it to the total.

Cook's utensils are artisan tools. Forge Dwarf's actual artisan time and Standard-to-Exceptional quality bridge may apply within their reviewed scopes. They do not waive ingredient freshness, formula/trade level, station/facility gates, calendar waiting, sleep/rest or storage. The one-workyear recipe uses the existing **1,920 active hours** overlay while preserving the source's null active-hours field; the eligible 25% time reduction operates on those work hours, not on the immutable source record.

Bound mixture is stabilized only inside its actual work order. It cannot be extracted as fresh stock, used in another order or sold as a generic raw-ingredient preservation service. Returned catalysts and legitimate recovered inputs keep their source identity, condition and accumulated age. No source-specific magical containment or lawful-harvest requirement is waived.

Successful finished meals start a **24-hour unprotected cooked-food age clock at craft completion**. At that deadline they become Spoiled directly, without an intermediate Degraded stage: no Cooking magic, meal nutrition credit or ordinary finished-meal market value. Existing mundane food preservation may pause age using its actual time, costs, container, checks and maximum lot size. Opening or repackaging never resets age. Spoiled food cannot be made Fresh by resealing or ordinary reheating. Consumption legally begun before expiry follows its committed-meal rule above.

Successful preparation neutralizes only unprinted incidental ingestion hazards of the recipe's ingredients **inside that finished serving**. It does not establish general poison immunity, purify unrelated stock, authorize harvesting, or change the ingredient's raw properties. The explicit failed-skewer profile below overrides that default. Contamination newly imposed by another actual effect uses its own rules and is not erased by the fact that cooking succeeded earlier.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Armor and shields
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Armor and shields

Choose one applicable AC formula. Light armor adds the full DEX modifier to its printed base. Medium adds `min(DEX modifier, 2)`, including a negative modifier. Heavy uses its fixed AC without positive or negative DEX. Explicit separate AC bonuses apply only when their own requirements are met.

One usable equipped shield contributes its printed bonus: buckler +1, shield +2, tower shield +3. No second shield bonus. Elven weave's printed Stealth advantage uses ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation. Dwarven plate is AC 18; its descriptive superior protection adds nothing. Scale mail's description adds no slashing resistance. Tower shield adds no unprinted cover or additional movement penalty.

**Nonproficient worn armor.** Retain V6 disadvantage on STR/DEX ability checks, saving throws and attacks. Core replaces the older casting prohibition: spells remain permitted, but an RP-priced spell costs +1 RP once per cast and concentration checks/saves have disadvantage. Multiple nonproficient armor pieces never multiply this surcharge. A normal 0-RP spell using the RP price interface can cost 1 RP. Apply this ordinary price addition before the already reviewed eligible reductions and final Resonance Influence step.

**Nonproficient shield — new completion.** While using a shield without shield proficiency, apply the STR/DEX check/save/attack disadvantage. A shield alone adds neither Core's armor RP surcharge nor concentration disadvantage and does not prohibit casting. Core names worn armor for those casting penalties.

A charge-only ancestry spell, Oracle effect or other cast with no RP-price interface acquires no RP price or pool from nonproficient armor. Actual concentration still has disadvantage from nonproficient worn armor. Hands, spell components and other independent casting restrictions remain.

**Strength minimum — new completion.** If one or more equipped armor/shield records have a listed STR minimum you do not meet, reduce Speed by 10 feet total, minimum 0. This is not a minimum to equip; multiple deficient pieces do not stack the reduction. This penalty can coexist with Load/Burden.

The Dwarf's printed rule that Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor prevents this penalty when the deficient item is heavy armor. It does not waive Load/Burden, another movement penalty or a tower shield's separate STR minimum. If a table chooses V6's preserved optional encumbrance alternate, that alternate ignores the Armor Table Strength column; the active reviewed Load procedure is not that alternate.

| Equipment | Don | Doff |
|---|---|---|
| Light armor | 1 minute | 1 minute |
| Medium armor | 5 minutes | 1 minute |
| Heavy armor | 10 minutes | 5 minutes |
| Any shield | 1 Action | 1 Action |

One actual assisting creature halves doff time only; a shield still takes at least one Action. Additional helpers do not repeatedly halve it.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Fit and size

Equipment must fit its intended user. Small/Medium and Tiny fitted ordinary items retain the listed price, mass and profile in this candidate; fit creates no unprinted benefit. **New Large sizing:** ordinary armor, shields and weapons use twice the baseline price, twice the weight and twice generic structural HP, with the same AC, damage, reach and properties unless an exact source says otherwise.

A fixed creation package includes the necessary fitting without an added creation charge. Its sized baseline matters for replacement, resale and repair. On the wealth route, buy the fitted item at its actual sized price. Powerful Build changes only its expressly permitted carrying calculations, not item size or weapon damage. It does not resize equipment on transformation; the reviewed body/equipment rules govern that transition.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Speed arbitration
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Speed arbitration

**NEW:** Keep soft flat reductions, soft fractional reductions, explicit Speed0 controls, and Core Grappled/Restrained separate. Terrain changes movement cost; it is not a Speed penalty. “Hostile soft control” means an adverse control record regardless of whether an enemy, ally or the victim applied it.

1. Determine each possessed mode's Speed after compatible ordinary bonuses and systemic flat penalties (including serum/expedition Strain, serum side effects, cargo and stances). Their existing stacking rules still apply.
2. Evaluate every unsuppressed adverse soft-control record against that **same** pre-control Speed. Flat -10 gives `max(0, Speed-10)`; half gives `floor(Speed/2)`; use the exact registered formula for other records.
3. Use the lowest result. Different slows do not add unless an expressly reviewed source grants an exception. Keep all losing records and their independent deadlines.
4. Apply separately established global multipliers such as Exhaustion's half-Speed. Apply an active Hypermutation floor as specified below.
5. An explicit Speed0 state, Core Grappled/Restrained, Exhaustion5 or another actual immobilization overrides the numeric result. An unavailable mode remains unavailable. A separate prohibition on voluntary movement is not removed by a positive Speed.

Thus -10 and half on Speed30 yield15; Exhaustion then yields7. Two -10 records yield20, not10. Serum/expedition penalties remain independent system penalties, not competing hostile slow records. A minimum attached to a penalty cannot raise existing Speed: Iron Leash Aura uses `min(preSpeed, max(5, preSpeed-10))`.

Active adverse soft controls and explicit source Speed0 controls carry `eligibility.slowed-foe`; Core Grappled/Restrained alone, Prone, cargo, terrain and Exhaustion do not. A numerically overshadowed application still qualifies. Suppressed, expired or prevented applications do not.

Same owner/target/group/exact profile refreshes without adding magnitude or shortening its remaining deadline. Different magnitude/formula profiles retain separate deadlines within a group; a weaker later application cannot erase an unexpired stronger one. Removing/suppressing one record exposes any other valid record. Paid reapplication and source caps remain required. No arithmetic Speed result grants movement: the combat guide's common spent-movement ledger still applies.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Root, physical restraints and suppression
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Root, physical restraints and suppression

Root supplies Speed0 only; it does not inherently apply Restrained, Grappled, Incapacitated, Action/Reaction loss or a teleport ban. A Speed0 source not named Root receives no invented Root identity. Multiple zero records coexist; ending one does not end another.

Printed restraint saves, escape Actions, size/anatomy limits, concentration and relationship endpoints win. **NEW fallback only** for genuine physical Restrained with no explicit escape, no sufficient fixed endpoint and no special-cure requirement: Action STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against recorded applying DC, otherwise10, ends **one selected** record on success. An adjacent helper may instead use Action STR(Athletics). None of the supplied active restraints needs this fallback. A fixed endpoint alone excludes it. No generic cutting, helper or object-HP escape is added to magical-only restraints.

Net Bolt retains printed Action STR(Athletics) escape, net AC10/HP5, maximum3 rounds and Huge+ -10 replacement. Tinker Net Trap retains its printed repeat save/Action escape. Earthen Grip's grounded-target requirement is an application requirement; the source does not say moving/teleporting away ends it. It persists after a legal teleport until concentration, printed time or its Action escape ends it. Tyrant's Impale and Panther retain their explicit reach/separation/reversion relationship endings. If suppression permits escape beyond a required maintained reach, the source ends and cannot resume. An attached physical net otherwise persists through suppression and can resume until removed/destroyed/expired.

Immunity suppresses only covered components; clocks and relationship checks continue. Word of Binding's Silenced and Speed0 are independent for immunity, while its successful repeat save ends both. A suppressed record does not grant active eligibility hooks. Ending one restriction does not cure unrelated damage, marks or components on the same card.
